summary: Remote-shell relay: WebSocket channel drives local Claude Code / shell execution on installer host
details: The package's bin connects to a hardcoded WebSocket relay at wss://cho100.cn/mars-relay and pipes messages received from that channel into local child_process / pty invocations (Claude Code and shell), giving whoever controls the relay command execution on the host running the tool. The README frames this as a phone remotely taking over Claude Code after a QR pairing step, but the dataflow — inbound network messages driving local shell/PTY spawn — is a remote-shell backdoor: the relay operator, not just the paired phone, is in a position to issue commands to the installer's machine. The relay endpoint is a single hardcoded third-party host (cho100.cn) with no end-to-end authentication of the controller visible in the code, and no scoping of what commands can be run.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
